newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's August oil trade deficit narrows 38.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Peru's August oil trade deficit narrows 38.7 pct.

text.p: Peru's crude oil and oil product trade deficit narrowed 38.7 percent to $19 million, compared with the same month last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Tuesday.
The crude oil and oil products deficit rose 2.1 percent in the first eight months of the year to $191 million, compared with same period last year, the bank said in its weekly report.
August's imports of crude oil and oil products were $51 million, down from $53 million in the same month last year. Exports in August rose to $32 million from $22 million in the same month last year.
In the first eight months of the year, imports of crude oil and oil products rose 26.1 percent to $435 million. Exports rose 54.4 percent to $244 million, compared with the same period in 1995.
Peru's oil deficit swelled 134 percent to $323.2 million in 1995 compared with $138 million the previous year, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
